📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

It has been revealed that this was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

Trafford again! 👊🏻 An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J.

Recent findings suggest that this was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in.

There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

In a recent development, harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

Sources indicate that england have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

According to recent reports, the defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England revealed on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

They all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. Anderson demonstrated that he is one of the best midfielders in the world in the hour before his red card. Spain were without Rodri and in his absence his Manchester City successor was in control.

Tuchel encouraged his players to mount a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave, but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Such was the pressure, the Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón abandoned the usual build-up strategy and launched his goal-kicks to the halfway line.

According to recent reports, even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. It took them a while to manage the discomfort of being denied the ball, and the familiar rapid incursions and switches of play. The counter-attacking switch from the early period pressing Spain in their own area yielded the penalty from which Kane scored the first.

Rice’s delivery was on the money and Rogers also managed to step in front of Aymeric Laporte to allow Konsa a free run on to the header.

According to recent reports, it was only another Jarell Quansah error that got Spain back into the game. His mistake allowed Fermin López to play in Yamal for the run in which he was fouled by Anderson for the red card and the subsequent penalty.

Quansah is trying to do the hardest thing asked of a centre-half: play the ball out from the back. His red card in Mexico City and his mistake on Thursday against Croatia have not helped. Nevertheless, John Stones had a tricky start in an England shirt and developed into one of the team’s most important figures.

From another breakaway Yamal crossed for the substitute Williams to score Spain’s second. They would push again but England held on.

Thomas Tuchel praised England’s “statement win” that ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and secured top spot ahead of the world champions in the Nations League.

Tuchel and Declan Rice revealed they had both believed England would end Spain’s long unbeaten streak, and their confidence proved well-founded.

“This was of course a statement victory,” Tuchel mentioned. “I’m happy the players felt so confident. I felt it as well. I also had the same belief [that England would win]. I think we felt it from each other.

Recent findings suggest that “The result followed the performance. I think it was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, in all aspects of the game.”.

Tuchel described the nature of England’s win as “the Azteca reloaded” in reference to the World Cup victory over Mexico, but felt the win in Madrid was the best of his reign as head coach.

He said: “Yeah [it was the best performance of his reign so far], given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. They were unbeaten in 43 games. So putting a performance out there in Madrid, in this environment, that was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

It has been revealed that “The last half an hour felt like Azteca reloaded, to be honest. Again, it was a beautiful week. The commitment to get better is on the highest level.

“I noted it many times, I love these players and I love the mentality .We’re building something and that was the next step. It was an amazing atmosphere. I will bottle it up for sure and then unfortunately we have to wait until the quarter-final.”.

"Without the red card, I think we had a clear win" 🗣️ Thomas Tuchel gives his verdict on England's performance against Spain that ended their 43-match unbeaten run https://t.co/rPef21Gtov.

Asked what beating Spain can do for England’s belief, before the draw for the quarter-finals of the Nations League on Friday, Tuchel stated: “You want confidence, not only through results, but confidence through performance and the result follows.

According to recent reports, “That’s the ideal process and that’s what we got. We got it through the whole campaign of the Nations League, we trusted the process and improved our game and took steps forward match by match.

“We had a fantastic result and performance in Croatia followed up by a very good performance at home against Czechia. We then got our homework done against Croatia three days ago and that’s what we always wanted.

“We wanted to come back and compete on the highest level and see how far we can push our limits and how far we can push the opponent with the way we want to play and stay true to our identity. The team did excellent.”.

England survived a Spanish fightback to round off their Nations League group-stage campaign in style with a 3-2 win over the world champions in Madrid.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored for the visitors with James Trafford pulling off a series of saves to prevent the hosts drawing level.

The message from the manager after the Croatia game was so positive. The message from the boys, everyone pushing together, knowing that we’re going to come here and not sit back and hit them on the counter.

“We knew from the first minute - our first 10 minutes was probably the best we’ve played in a 10-minute spell. Pressure, pressure, pressure, we could have had two or three.

“The red card changes the course of the game as it could have been a couple more [England goals] if I’m being honest. If we don’t go down to 10, we get more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, more space. Then you start to see tackles flying like we saw in the second half.

“Ten men for half an hour. To win it 3-2 against that team, unbeaten in 43, is a massive thing.”.

The Football Association considered a legal challenge to Gianni Infantino’s eligibility to stand for a fourth term as Fifa president but decided it would not succeed, its chair Debbie Hewitt has remarked.

Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president and Fifa Council member, was not on the Council in 2022 when it took a decision to discount Infantino’s first term from 2016 to 2019 from the three-term limit set out in Fifa’s statutes, effectively clearing him to stand again next year.

The FA was asked by human rights group FairSquare’s Reboot campaign to challenge Infantino’s eligibility, but as first reported by the BBC, Hewitt has responded to say the FA had already considered it and decided against it.

“The FA has explored the possibility of challenging Mr Infantino’s eligibility to run for a further term as Fifa president but does not consider that such a challenge would secure the outcome sought,” Hewitt wrote in a letter seen by the Press Association.

Sources indicate that “Ultimately the process followed Fifa’s governance and led to an outcome where Mr Infantino’s part term was disregarded for the purposes of maximum term limits. Having considered the process in detail, we do not believe that a challenge would succeed.”.

The FA declined to comment on the letter, but it is understood the exploration of a legal challenge to the term limits took place when other efforts to extract information from Fifa about the controversial World Cup private investor blueprint and the Folarin Balogun disciplinary case had been exhausted.

The FA was the only national association which objected to changes in Uefa’s statutes in 2024 which have now allowed Aleksander Ceferin to stand for a fourth term as its president next year.

Infantino has stated he intends to stand for a fourth term at the Fifa Congress in Morocco in March and appears well placed to win, with the deadline for candidates to be submitted having now passed.

Uefa said in August it had lost confidence in Infantino over the private investor proposal and would work to identify a credible candidate to stand against him.

On Monday it was unveiled French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo had the backing of national associations on the Uefa executive committee and European members of the Fifa Council, including Hewitt.

She intends to travel to Zurich to scrutinise documents related to the World Cup private investor plan, following an offer to do so made by Fifa’s secretary general Mattias Grafstrom on 2 November.

However, that trip is understood to be dependent on the conditions Fifa seek to impose and the terms of any non-disclosure agreements it insists must be signed.

Fifa confirmed on Thursday morning that three candidates had been proposed by the national FAs – Infantino, Diallo and Kohzo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association.

Fifa mentioned the candidates’ names would now be submitted to its electoral committee for eligibility checks, and that national associations would be notified no later than 18 February on the final list of admitted candidates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak.

Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result.

Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so.

But for all the familiarity and continuity for the Socceroos – five players who were there when Son Heung-min broke Australian hearts featured in Friday’s win – being back in Doha rams home just how much has changed for this team, and how well and truly into a upcoming era we are.

Tony Popovic occupies the dugout these days, after the defeat to Korea arguably represented the beginning of the end of Arnold’s tenure by sparking a fatigue that would culminate in a downturn in results and his resignation later that year.

Sources indicate that nestory Irankunda, the rapidly emerging star of Popovic’s team who now has eight international goals to his name, was about to suffer a 4-0 defeat against the Central Coast Mariners nearly three years ago. Alessandro Circati was left out of the Socceroos squad to ensure he retained his place in the Parma side seeking to secure promotion to Serie A. Paul Okon-Engstler, Patrick Beach and Lucas Herrington were all yet to play senior football.

Industry observers note that these players, who all started against Qatar, are emerging cornerstones of a upcoming Socceroos setup that fielded the World Cup’s youngest side in North America, before flashing signs of further growth against Brazil in September. On Friday, this talented group bullied the two-time defending Asian champions on their own turf in the first-half, putting the game to bed before Popovic swung the changes and things got disjointed after half-time.

According to recent reports, there is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality. Of players bringing to the national team the lessons they’ve learned not just in the green and gold, but also in their experiences at bigger, more demanding clubs and leagues – in part because of the platform they’ve been offered by Popovic.

All of which could make it serendipitous if Tuesday’s game against Jordan, at the symbolic home of his predecessor, proves to be the end of the Popovic era.

The players aren’t going anywhere but with his contract situation still up in the air, it could well prove to be Popovic’s last game in charge of the Socceroos if he doesn’t agree to an extension. Given the postponement of January’s Asian Cup, there may not be the send-off he might have envisioned. Instead, a 12,000-seat stadium – unlikely to be very full – will host a hastily relocated friendly that’s entire raison d’être has vanished.

Remarkably, after sensitive discussions to relocate Tuesday’s game after player resistance to travelling to Amman, in line with DFAT advice, Doha could once again be pressed into action to serve as a historic backdrop for the Socceroos, just as a pandemic already saw it become the site of many a moment of distinction.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz got a birthday cake at the UN climate summit in Turkey this week. But he wasn't there to eat it. Meanwhile, in Berlin, climate activists marked his 71st birthday on Friday with a symbolic chocolate cake. Their message: they too want to reach that age on a livable planet.

In a recent development, fridays for Future is taking its demands to German streets. Demonstrations were planned in more than 70 German cities on Friday, November 13.

Under the slogan "Pay your climate debt," protesters in the German capital demanded more funding for climate protection and adaptation in developing countries, alongside a global phase-out of coal, oil and gas.

Germany provided €4.7 billion ($5.2 billion) in federal budget funds for international climate financing in 2025 — below its €6 billion pledge.

Recent findings suggest that but the protest movement is no longer drawing the crowds it once did. In September 2019, Fridays for Future mobilized an estimated 1.4 million people across Germany. Five years later, that figure fell to around 75,000 at a comparable nationwide strike.

Industry observers note that this comes as broader youth frustration with German politics grows. "I don't feel addressed by the chancellor unfortunately," Kim, a protester in Berlin, told DW.

From military service to affordable housing and climate policy, younger Germans are questioning whether their concerns are being heard.

Industry observers note that A recent nationwide poll found that 82% of Germans believe politicians do not adequately represent young people's interests. Among 18- to 34-year-olds, just 5% trust Merz's conservatives to champion their concerns, compared with 3% for their Social Democratic coalition partners.

According to recent reports, merz is not the first German chancellor to miss a UN climate summit. And smaller demonstrations do not necessarily mean young Germans care less about climate change. But the contrast is striking: while the climate movement struggles to mobilize, dissatisfaction among younger voters extends well beyond environmental policy.

Julian Reichelt, formerly the editor-in-chief of Germany's top-selling tabloid Bild, says he was the target of an arson attack after his car was set on fire and largely destroyed in Berlin.

Now editor-in-chief of the right-wing online portal Nius that he co-founded, Reichelt said the arson attack took place in the Charlottenburg district of the German capital overnight.

It has been revealed that police confirmed the car was intentionally set alight, saying a passerby reported it shortly after 2 a.m. that morning. However, they did not name a suspect or potential personal motive at first, saying only that the fire department responded and extinguished the fire.

"It is completely clear that this was a targeted attack," Reichelt stated, calling it an "attempt at intimidation against fresh free media that stand up against this left-wing extremism.".

Similar arson attacks several years ago targeted cars belonging to a columnist for another Berlin newspaper, B.Z., with a left-wing group claiming responsibility in one case.

Industry observers note that that said, Berlin also has a more general and fairly well documented problem with arson and vandalism targeting cars, with an average of roughly two a night being set alight in the capital city over recent years. Vandalism and insurance fraud are the most common reasons more generally.

Reichelt was fired from his prominent job at Bild in 2021 amid allegations of sexual harassment, accusations he always denied and referred to as a "smear campaign.".

Lawmakers in the Bundestag have approved reforms that will provide additional powers to Germany's domestic and external intelligence agencies.

The changes will strengthen both the external Federal Intelligence Service (BND) and domestic intelligence service the BfV, formally titled the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

The law passed fairly comfortably in the federal Bundestag lower house of parliament, with 309 votes in favor, 190 against and 71 abstentions.

The BfV will be granted powers beyond intelligence gathering and monitoring individuals, such as being able to secretly enter homes or take action against explosives or weapons.

In the case of the BND, it will be granted additional operational intervention powers, for instance moving to disable servers belonging to state-sponsored hacker groups abroad.

The changes aim to respond to intensified and evolving threats from foreign intelligence services and their partners, and to reduce dependency on information supplied by friendly foreign intelligence services.

Opposition parties have accused the government of abolishing or weakening the separation between the police and intelligence services — a sensitive and closely monitored distinction in German society, because of the legacy both of Adolf Hitler's Nazi regime and of the secret police services in Communist East Germany during the Cold War.

Friedrich Merz has noted during his visit to Dublin that Germany and Europe's position in future peace talks for Ukraine is "set.".

Following the talks in Abu Dhabi this week between Ukraine and Russia brokered by the US, which also involved European representatives at times, Merz said further negotiations were now planned.

"In the coming weeks there should now be concrete peace talks in which Europe is represented," Merz told reporters in Dublin amid an informal meeting of EU leaders.

He mentioned that "provisionally" this might involve the same "group of Europeans" who had participated in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.

"Germany is set in there, that is completely clear," he noted.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's call to link EU budget negotiations to the provision of assistance to Ukraine, which faced hefty criticism at home, has found some backing amid European Political Community meetings and an AI summit in Dublin.

Merz, who has been leading the charge to find savings in the next EU budget, remarked doing so could ensure stronger contributions to helping Ukraine from all EU member states.

Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michal stated during the meeting in Dublin that he approved of Merz's suggestion "that support for Ukraine is also a part of our core security and our core financing.".

He stated that members who wanted a upcoming EU budget should contribute.

Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs, meanwhile, remarked he agreed completely with Merz.

"We must all pull in the same direction. All of Europe must do its part," he said.

Luxembourg's Luc Frieden also said that "we must all stand behind Ukraine" and added that collective financial commitments should be a part of this.

As the largest economy and most populous country in the EU, Germany is the largest overall contributor both to the EU budget and to assistance for Ukraine.

Countries that tend to be so-called net beneficiaries of the EU budget, rather than net contributors to it, tend to be more reticent to cut spending plans.

Hosts Ireland, in a tricky position as the holders of the rotating presidency of the EU trying to broker a deal on the next seven-year budget, said it had concerns about adding an additional factor to the stalled talks, as the current budget's expiry at the end of 2027 starts to draw near.

Industry observers note that "But I do understand why this is happening," Taoiseach (or prime minister) Micheal Martin stated in Dublin. "Some countries have made considerable contributions and they want all EU member states to contribute financially to the support for Ukraine.".

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) was critical of both the spending and the fundraising plans in the 2027 budget, claiming without showing its workings that it would be able to do more with less by making swingeing cuts in various key areas.

Budget policy spokesman Michael Espendiller said the budget meant "more debts and more taxes and more burdens for the taxpayer.".

He accused the Christian Democrats of breaking key election pledges by raising taxes on alcohol and tobacco. He then complained that despite this, there was not enough money for the promised electricity tax cut.

"If you put it into figures, the federal government will be taking out almost €400,000 (around $440,000) every minute in upcoming debt," Espendiller said, calling for an end to what he called a spiral of debt.

He claimed that the AfD would have able to complete its budget with new debt of just €63 billion, not roughly €210 billion, while simultaneously providing tax relief of around €44 billion.

Espendiller said this would be achieved with wide-reaching cuts in several core areas of spending: climate protection, contributing to the EU budget and other EU funding, asylum-related spending, international development aid, and weapons deliveries and other assistance to Ukraine.

It's unclear to what extent these proposed cuts would be feasible or legal, or what domestic or international implications they might have, or whether they'd save anything like the amount the AfD asserts in practice.

Politicians on the Bundestag budget committee burned the proverbial candle at both ends heading into Friday morning, trying to finalize details of the federal government's spending intends for 2027 before the year's end.

The session took over 15 hours, and already politicians are talking about areas where they still see room for further improvement or alteration — but the document does at least stand in such a form in which it can take effect without too many complications.

Including all spending aims, in the core budget and from the so-called "special funds" for infrastructure and military modernization, newly introduced debt constitutes around a third of oultays.

In total, the blueprint is to take out upcoming debt worth just over €210 billion ($233 billion), while taking in a little less than €400 billion in taxes.

Recent findings suggest that that's the second-highest level of new debt in the post-war history of the Federal Republic of Germany. Even at the height of the COVID pandemic in 2021, new debt was only slightly higher, at €215.4 billion.

We'll likely be returning to the various details of and reactions to this story throughout the morning.

The environmentalist Greens took aim at Chancellor Merz for not delivering on a promise to reduce taxes on electricity in the final budget.

"The major promise that Chancellor Merz made a few days ago, sinking electricity taxes for everyone, this promise remains a broken promise," party co-leader Britta Hasselmann remarked on ZDF television on Friday.

"It was possible to find a way at short notice for several other things in this budget," she noted.

"I think this demonstrates the inadequate planning and the weak leadership of the chancellor," Hasselmann said.

She added that the CDU forcing a delay to the planned sugar tax at short notice was further evidence of the planning shortcomings.

A budget expert at the party, Sebastian Schäfer, similarly alleged a "leadership vacuum in this coalition government," saying that what was put forward was less a budget and more a "wooden shack wihtout foundations.".

The Left Party's budget policy spokesman Dietmar Bartsch has lamented a "knot garden of debt, tricks and delays," accusing the coalition of not conducting "responsible budgetary policy.".

Despite criticizing the debt levels, Bartsch also remarked it was "deeply unserious" to float electricity tax relief but then withdraw the proposal.

He remarked this would have cost less money than the federal government's initiative to buy a share of the arms company KNDS. He also said it was unacceptable for the center-left Social Democrats to be celebrating just because "the odd welfare cut is not happening.".

Ines Schwerdtner, co-leader of the party that firmly opposes defense spending and is at best lukewarm on NATO membership, remarked the record spending demonstrated that money was not as tight as Merz's government made out.

It has been revealed that "The debt brake is suspended for weapons, but for housing and electricity taxes they scrimp for every euro," Schwerdtner said. "The money is there, this government is just distributing it completely incorrectly.".

Schwerdtner, herself a member of the budget committed in the Bundestag, called it a "budget of naivete.".

More on this morning's top story in Berlin, the 2027 budget being signed off.

As the CDU calls for further savings, the Social Democrats say that the energy tax relief recently touted by Chancellor Friedrich Merz "would have to be financed with additional debts.".

Ahead of Thursday's marathon talks, Merz had said he hoped to introduce the tax relief amid the stress caused by concerns including the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

The SPD's Dirk Wiese said the junior coalition partners were "not disinclined to pave the way for the electricity tax relief," but not by making cuts elsewhere.

Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil of the SPD had stated he did not see enough fiscal wiggle room to enable the desired tax break.

Bremen's mayor Andreas Bovenshulte, also a Social Democrat, remarked that while he would have welcomed the relief, other decisions meant it wasn't possible.

"For that, a serious financing source would have been required, for instance with a plastic or sugar of windfall tax," Bovenschulte noted, in reference to either delayed or proposed but rejected looks to potentially increase tax revenues.

German defense industry startup Quantum Systems mentioned its drones were operational worldwide once again, including with the Bundeswehr military, after a cyberattack by "hostile actors" last month.

The company had announced the cyberattack on Thursday, amid reporting from the Financial Times that also said the Bundeswehr had grounded its drones from the company.

Sources indicate that "The fleet is operating normally around the globe — including Germany and the Bundeswehr," a Quantum Systems spokesperson stated in an emailed statement to the Reuters news agency. "The Bundeswehr was the only customer to ground their systems as a precaution.".

The company, based near Munich, had earlier remarked it uncovered an "active cyberattack" by hostile actors.

"The threat was contained thanks to the swift response of our IT and security teams in close and transparent collaboration with the authorities," it remarked in a statement, adding there was no risk for end users and operators using its unmanned systems.

Quantum drones are used by Ukrainian armed forces in their defensive war against Russia, among others.

In a recent development, "Companies at the forefront of supporting Ukraine are being targeted precisely because our work is critically relevant to customers' security," the company mentioned. "Being aware of this responsibility, Quantum Systems has mitigation aims in place and strives to fulfil the highest standard of data and system security.".

He identified one "weak point" after the overnight negotiations.

"We have not yet saved enough, we still need to save a lot more," he mentioned.

Middelberg noted that in his view the government would not be able to "collect the funds," because that would put too much tax strain on people and businesses.

Therefore, he said, "the government must make cutbacks.".

Middelberg acepted that it wasn't clear how to do this, speculating that "perhaps there are subsidies or some other things" that could be ripe to be trimmed.

He said the leadership of the coalition government's CDU/CSU and Social Democrats would "consider this question very closely once more.".

The German government statistics agency Destatis has published new figures on insolvency filings for the month of August.

A total of 2,067 companies registered insolvencies with German courts during the month, Destatis stated, 4.4% more than in the same month in 2025.

The data operates on something of a delay, because the government tracks when courts grant the status, which can be almost three months after the initial application at times.

The increase has been a rolling trend this year. From January to August, 17,252 companies have filed for insolvency, 6.6% more than in the same period last year.

However, the total sum of debts forgiven in insolvency proceedings is actually quite considerably lower than in the first eight months of last year, at €25.9 billion ($28.7 billion) rather than €37.2 billion, because fewer large companies have gone bust.

More individuals are also filing for bankruptcy protection than in 2025, although the rise is somewhat less sharp. In August, 6,301 people gained insolvency protection, 2.8% more than last August. For January through August, the year-on-year increase is more modest, at 1.2%.

Politicians on the Bundestag budget committee burned the proverbial candle at both ends heading into Friday morning, trying to finalize details of the federal government's spending intends for 2027 before the year's end.

Here are a few of the core statistics:.

In a recent development, moin! Here's hoping you slept more and better than the Bundestag's budget committee. Or if not, at least let's hope that you had more fun.

Its members worked towards the dawn in a session lasting over 15 hours, trying to iron out the last wrinkles in spending plans for 2027.

The proverbial white smoke emerged at around 6 in the morning in Berlin, with word of a finalized agreement.

If you were tired of talk and criticism of the "debt brake" and the "black zero" (a promise not to take any latest debts) in the years following the eurozone debt crisis, rest assured we can assign such chatter to the history books for now.

The borrowing plans for 2027 — if you incorporate upcoming debt taken out as part of so-called "special funds," for instance for the military and infrastructure, rather than as part of the core budget — are the second highest in the history of post-war Germany.

The country only took out more new debt in 2021, at the height of the COVID pandemic and even then it was very close indeed.

We'll bring you more news and reactions on this, and whatever else breaks around the country, as Friday develops.

#36352. On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (708 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars.
  • NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9.
  • Sources indicate that when Mariner 9 got to Mars, it arrived in the middle of a dust storm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet.

NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9. Those flybys indicated that Mars had a cratered surface, so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds.

Sources indicate that when Mariner 9 got to Mars, it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes.

Industry observers note that one volcano, Olympus Mons, is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris. This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona.

Industry observers note that mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time.

Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so.

Industry observers note that the NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description. (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.).

But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore.

Industry observers note that mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission.

The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide.

"The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA noted in an overview.

Industry observers note that in all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars.

It has been revealed that by February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed the Ukrainian national football federation for the failed drugs test which saw him banned from football for 20 months.

Mudryk tested positive for the banned substance meldonium in 2024, and was initially banned for four years by the Football Association. He successfully appealed against the length of his ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, and returned to football in July 2026.

The Tottenham winger, who is on loan from Chelsea, spoke to Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, and remarked he blamed “the environment in the Ukrainian national team” for his suspension.

According to recent reports, “I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.”.

He mentioned he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which “points to the fact it was in a national team camp”.

Mudryk mentioned that he received little support from association president Andriy Shevchenko or the rest of the organisation.

He said he cried and turned to alcohol in the immediate aftermath of the suspension.

Sources indicate that “It was a bolt from the blue. I couldn't believe it [the positive test] was true,” he mentioned. “It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on falling. It hit me very hard, mentally.”.

Mudryk added he had spent millions of pounds on legal fees as well as personal training and physiotherapy in order to continue his career while not having access to facilities at Chelsea.

The Ukrainian football federation has been contacted for comment.

A long wait, some magic and that smile: Ronaldinho savours Ravenna debut at 46

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, indicated glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side.
  • It may have been the longest buildup in world football.
  • But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was, not only in the squad, but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brazilian legend, an investor at Serie C club, indicated glimpses of old brilliance as he played 45 minutes for the promotion-chasing side.

It may have been the longest buildup in world football. In June, the former Barcelona and Brazil legend Ronaldinho was unveiled by the Serie C side Ravenna to make his comeback at the age of 46 – 11 years after his last official game. Then silence.

But on a chilly November day on the eastern coast of Italy, there he was, not only in the squad, but in the starting XI for the eagerly anticipated derby against Forlì as Ravenna chase promotion.

Industry observers note that the Ravenna manager, Andrea Mandorlini, deployed Ronaldinho in a central position, just behind the striker Simone Rabbi. The Brazilian held his position well, but was slow to get going. As the game progressed, he warmed up and showed his excellent skills; some things do not appear to change. Ronaldinho touched the ball 25 times, took three corners – one of which nearly led to a Ravenna goal – and initiated the move that led to the hosts taking the lead in the 35th minute.

Having trained with the team just once, whether he plays again remains to be seen. But he had already sprinkled some magic on a club and a region that has not made headlines in years. He played the first half as Ravenna won 2-0 to stay second in the division’s Group B (the Italian third tier is divided into three regional sections). Only the group winners earn promotion and Ravenna trail Spezia by six points.

Whatever happens for the remainder of the season this has put the club back on the football map. Ravenna’s highest finish was eighth in Serie B, in 1996-97, but this match was broadcast live by Sky Sports in Italy and shown in several other countries. It even appeared on the giant screens in New York’s Times Square, where the club’s owners, the Cipriani family, have built much of their international reputation through Harry’s Bar.

The town’s mayor, Alessandro Barattoni, who, as always, was watching the game from the stands, stated: “A champion like Ronaldinho, a world football icon, brings great visibility and today is an opportunity for us to showcase Ravenna around the world, from our stadium. It is something latest for us and together with the club the municipality will try to understand how this can have a positive impact on the town.”.

It has been revealed that the local community had been excited at the prospect of Ronaldinho representing the club, but there was some regret, too. “It would have been nice if he had come to take a stroll around the city, among the people who live here and own the shops,” the barista Barbara said before the game.

So how did he end up here? The Brazilian is a friend of Ignazio Cipriani, the owner of the Giallorossi. Lorenzo Tonetti and Ariedo Braida, old acquaintances from Ronaldinho’s time at Milan, are also part of the club. They convinced him to become an investor in the club and to pull on his boots again. In addition, Ravenna are now wearing his R10 sportswear line and one of the stands bears the same name.

In a recent development, ravenna are aiming high. Cipriani has never hidden the fact he is aiming for Serie A, which is ambitious for a city with a population of 156,000. And Sunday brought hope, Dinho stepping on to the pitch in a gold-trimmed kit picked by the club to celebrate his arrival (and available for sale at €120). His hair was kept in check by a black headband and he was wearing gloves on a chilly afternoon. On his back, the No 10, something more than just a number for him, the man who became a global hero thanks to his extraordinary skill and contagious smile.

A younger generation has been able to discover Ronaldinho’s genius through the endless supply of online videos showcasing his greatest moments. Children who have never seen him play know his tricks and signature moves, while their parents can relive an era of football they may feel no longer exists.

It has been revealed that “Dad, was he strong?” a young girl asked her father as they walked hand in hand towards the stadium. “Yes, he was strong. Actually, he is strong,” he corrected himself.

One family had left Rome at 5am and travelled the 350km north just because their son had watched Ronaldinho on YouTube and wanted to see him live. Others had travelled even further, with supporters arriving from Turkey and Canada.

In a recent development, ronaldinho hahas scored 299 professional goals, but his landmark 300th on his return was not to be. However, in front of a record attendance of 6,743 the way he initiated the move for Giulio Donati’s goal was ample reward for those who had turned up. Donati made his Serie A debut on 29 August 2010 for Lecce, at San Siro, against Milan, marking the Brazilian that day.

Sources indicate that as Ronaldinho walked off at half-time, he was surrounded by a media scrum. After the game, he spoke of his desire to play again. “It all went by too rapidly,” he said. “Football is like that, it’s always been like that for me.”.

Who knows, perhaps he enjoyed himself so much that he wants to extend his career even further. “I don’t know, but if the president calls me, I’ll come back. It’s always a pleasure to play, I told him: ‘when he needs me, I’m there’.”.

Mandorlini was effusive too. “We’re here and we’re truly proud to have been the architects of this match you played in,” he told the Brazilian. “So, if you want to play another one, that’s fine.”.

Recent findings suggest that who knows what the future holds? For now, Ravenna fans will always have this: a day when a true legend connected people from around the world and allowed them, for one afternoon, to dream.

Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

Editor’s Note:  This article was originally published by The Art Newspaper, an editorial partner of CNN Style.

Kwame Brathwaite, the pioneering activist and photographer whose work helped define the aesthetics of the “Black is Beautiful” movement of the 1960s and beyond, died on April 1, aged 85.

His son, Kwame Brathwaite, Jr, revealed his father’s death in an Instagram post that read in part, “I am deeply saddened to share that my Baba, the patriarch of our family, our rock and my hero has transitioned.”.

Brathwaite’s work has been the subject of resurgent interest from curators, historians and collectors in recent years, and his first major institutional retrospective, which was organized by the Aperture Foundation, made its debut in 2019 at the Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles before touring the country.

Sources indicate that brathwaite was born in 1938 to Barbadian immigrants, in what he referred to as “the People’s Republic of Brooklyn” in Upcoming York, though his family moved from there to Harlem and then to the South Bronx when Brathwaite was 5 years old. He attended the School of Industrial Art (now the High School of Art and Design) and, according to profiles of Brathwaite in T Magazine and Vice, was drawn to photography by two moments. The first was in August of 1955, when a 17-year-old Brathwaite encountered David Jackson’s haunting photograph of a brutalized Emmett Till in his open casket. The second was in 1956, when — after he and his brother Elombe co-founded the African Jazz Arts Society and Studios (AJASS) — Brathwaite saw a young man taking photos in a dark jazz club without the use of a flash, and his mind became alight with possibility.

According to recent reports, using a Hasselblad medium-format camera, Brathwaite attempted to do the same, learning to work with limited light in a manner that enhanced the visual narrative of his imagery. He would soon also develop a darkroom technique that enriched and deepened how Black skin would appear in his photography, honing the practice in a small darkroom in his Harlem apartment. Brathwaite went on to photograph jazz legends performing throughout the 1950s and ’60s, including Miles Davis, John Coltrane, Thelonious Monk and others.

“You want to get the feeling, the mood that you’re experiencing when they’re playing,” Brathwaite told Aperture Magazine in 2017. “That’s the thing. You want to capture that.”.

A 106-year-old from the Philippines is Vogue's oldest ever cover model.

By the early 1960s, alongside the rest of AJASS, Brathwaite began using his photography and organizing prowess to consciously push back against whitewashed, Eurocentric beauty standards. The group came up with the concept of the Grandassa Models, young Black women whom Brathwaite would photograph, celebrating and accentuating their features. In 1962, AJASS organized “Naturally ’62”, a fashion show held in a Harlem club called the Purple Manor and featuring the models. The show would go on to be held regularly until 1992. In 1966, Brathwaite married his wife Sikolo, a Grandassa Model whom he had met on the street the year prior when he asked if he could take her portrait. The two remained married for the rest of Brathwaite’s life.

By the 1970s, Brathwaite’s focus on jazz shifted to other forms of popular Black music. In 1974, he traveled to Africa with the Jackson Five to document their tour, also photographing the historic “Rumble in the Jungle” boxing match between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in what’s now the Democratic Republic of Congo that same year. Commissions in this era also saw Brathwaite photographing Nina Simone, Stevie Wonder, Sly and the Family Stone, Bob Marley and other music legends.

Creating for community: The Black designers placing identity and heritage at the center of their brands.

Throughout the ensuing decades, Brathwaite continued to explore and develop his mode of photography, all through the lens of the “Black is Beautiful” ethos. In 2016, Brathwaite joined the roster of Philip Martin Gallery in Los Angeles, and he was continuing to photograph commissions as recently as 2018, when he shot artist and stylist Joanne Petit-Frère for The Fresh Yorker.

Industry observers note that T Magazine’s 2021 profile, published on the occasion of Brathwaite’s retrospective traveling to the Blanton Museum of Art in Austin, Texas, noted that the photographer’s health was failing such that he was unable to be interviewed for the article. A separate exhibition, “Kwame Brathwaite: Things Well Worth Waiting For,” is presently on view at the Art Institute of Chicago, where it will remain until July 24.

Vincent Kompany states he is back in “very good health” as he prepares to make his return to the Bayern Munich dugout for the first time since collapsing at training.

Kompany was hospitalised after collapsing at a reserve team training session on 23 October and was diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

He missed five Bayern games as the club prioritised his health, with assistant coach Aaron Danks taking the reins and going unbeaten during that period.

But after returning to the club’s training ground during the international break, Kompany is raring to make his managerial comeback and take charge of his first game since drawing 2-2 with Arsenal a month ago.

“I was grateful for the support,” Kompany noted. “It was very intense. At the time, it was a upcoming experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly.

“I received immediate support from the club and from the doctors. I’m very grateful.

“I’m in very good health. We’ve done lots of tests, all of which have come back clear.”.

The Belgian was sporting a sling on his left arm after injuring his shoulder during the collapse.

Kompany remarked the incident prompted him to think differently about his health and that he “perhaps didn't listen closely” enough to his body when he returned for the Arsenal game despite having battled a viral infection that week.

Nevertheless, he revealed he had fun watching his team from a “fascinating” new perspective as Danks took charge, and claimed that Bayern's 2-0 win over Atletico Madrid earlier this month “was one of the finest moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn’t there”.

Sources indicate that “I’m coming off the longest holidays I ever had, it’s been the longest international break I ever had," Kompany stated. “It happened, it can happen to everyone, but you can learn from it.".

His first game back sees Bayern take on Koln on Friday evening, with the club top of the Bundesliga - ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (MAJOR) campaign called "The King's Return.".

SIGNIFICANT, a Christian group for footballers, has mentioned it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

It has been revealed that "Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he stated.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

"I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then remarked that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

According to recent reports, in Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp stated, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

Klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

Recent findings suggest that "We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

Why Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch face a fight for their Liverpool futures under Andoni Iraola

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No.
  • Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eighteen months ago, on his first return to Merseyside since leaving the club as manager the summer before, Jurgen Klopp spoke at a charity event at Liverpool Cathedral and singled out Dominik Szoboszlai for praise.

Probably the “best pressing player in Europe right now” was how the German described the Reds’ midfielder, who had played the season in the No. 10 role as Arne Slot’s side swept to the title.

Only nine months ago, Slot described the Hungarian as “maybe the best in the world in terms of pressing.” It’s quite the difference to today, when Szoboszlai’s pressing, now in a deeper role in midfield for Andoni Iraola, is coming into question.

“I think, for me, it’s about, in his mind, managing how much he presses and when to go, as opposed to just pressing for pressing’s sake,” Daniel Sturridge explained during Sky Sports' coverage of the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace.

“I’m not saying that he does that all the time, but I think the reason why Liverpool are open is because they don’t have someone who’s reading in front of the defence.”.

Recent findings suggest that that title-winning campaign two seasons ago saw Szoboszlai vital to everything Liverpool did well, with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch complementing each other - everything was seemingly perfectly balanced. Gravenberch played in a more restricted No. 6 role in front of defence, Mac Allister was the box-to-box No. 8, and Szoboszlai was the all-action, pressing No. 10.

Recent findings suggest that however, Slot worried that opponents had found out how to play against his team, and perhaps aware of losing Trent Alexander-Arnold’s unique creativity from deep, opted for a changed midfield set up. It actually began in the final away game of the title-winning season, away to Brighton, when Szoboszlai started in a two-man midfield alongside Gravenberch.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that and that’s how Slot continued the following campaign, having signed Florian Wirtz for the No. 10 role. It was a move that immediately had its sceptics. Promising Wirtz the central role, where he had never truly played before, seemed to leave Liverpool far more open in midfield.

Szoboszlai, though, became the first Liverpool midfielder since Steven Gerrard to score and assist 10 or more goals in a single campaign, scoring 13 and assisting 12 in 53 games across all competitions. He was named the Reds’ player of the season.

That, though, doesn’t tell the full story. Some fans were irked by the Hungarian’s manner, especially after a heavy defeat at Manchester City. The match-going supporter noticed how often he slowed play down and often encouraged others to do so. Slot saw it differently, saying: “He is an all-round player, an all-round midfielder, a modern midfielder in my opinion. I think this season he has improved his game on the ball. Off the ball, he is top three, four or five in the world.”.

With two years left to run on his contract, Szoboszlai was rewarded for his form with a new contract and named one of Iraola’s new vice-captains following the departures of Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah. Szoboszlai’s importance to the club could not have been clearer, and for many he was - and is - regarded as the most likely captain-in-waiting after Virgil van Dijk departs, whether that’s next summer or later.

But 10 league games into the upcoming season and it’s clear that Mac Allister is Iraola’s first-choice pick in his midfield two, and there are now growing calls for Trey Nyoni to be the player alongside the Argentine.

In a recent development, the pairing of Gravenberch and Szoboszlai was woefully exposed on the opening day at Newcastle, with the Dutchman finding himself very much out of favour once Mac Allister was back available after his later return due to the World Cup. But Mac Allister and Szoboszlai together also appears to lack balance, or understanding of when to press in Iraola’s system. “Both of the midfielders, whether it’s Mac Allister or Szoboszlai, have a tendency to vacate that space in front of the defence because of the press the manager wants to do,” Sturridge noted, accurately.

Injury to Szoboszlai during the last international break opened the door for teenager Nyoni's major break, including his first league start against Arsenal and his first time starting three consecutive matches. The reviews have been unanimous. The player who was handed his debut by Klopp at 16 has mightily impressed.

Nyoni’s first thought is always to play forward, capable of playing quick, direct passes into the attackers and splitting midfield in doing so. Some supporters see this as a stark contrast to Szoboszlai, who often runs with the ball or slows play and opts for a less positive pass.

Industry observers note that nyoni is also impressing off the ball, adept at tackling and comfortable dropping into the defensive line to start attacks from deep. The youngster explained Iraola’s instructions recently as being “as soon as you get the ball, it’s just play forward.”.

“Trey is very good on the ball, very calm, he reads the situations well,” Iraola praised in pre-season. “We’re forcing him in the work without the ball, in the press, and he is absolutely doing very well. I think the timings of the jumps are very good. He is always confident on the ball so we encourage him.”.

According to recent reports, the upcoming boss is clearly a huge fan of the player, who was the subject of a late £30 million bid from Nottingham Forest in the summer and who fellow teenage prodigy Rio Ngumoha claims “definitely still has another level to go. You guys haven’t even seen him at his top, top level.”.

It has been revealed that on the bench for the Palace game, having started the previous three in a row - including away to Fenerbahce where he bagged his first goal - Nyoni’s involvement in Liverpool's third as sub at Selhurst Park underlined exactly what his strengths are. He read the pass from Tyrick Mitchell inside his own box, intercepting with his left foot, before looking up and immediately playing a quick ball out to Alexander Isak with his right foot that completely split the Palace midfield and started the attack that ended with the Swede pulling the trigger.

Industry observers note that two touches was all it took from Nyoni. Technically, it was superb; the vision and execution perfect. It had some supporters making comparisons to Fabinho or Thiago. There is an argument that Nyoni’s passing style gets more from all the forwards, who clearly benefit when they receive the ball quickly, rather than once opposition defences have been able to get back behind the ball.

Liverpool have struggled against so-called low blocks for the past 18 months, since losing the qualities of a certain Alexander-Arnold (and more recently Salah) - Nyoni offers a much-needed solution to the creative dearth.

That, though, leaves a huge question of Szoboszlai - and Gravenberch, with both having signed fresh contracts this year.

“When a young player in midfield is playing ahead of them, that causes a problem,” Jamie Carragher expressed last week. “Basically, about where you’ve spent your money. It means you haven’t spent your money well enough.”.

Throw in reports of Liverpool’s interest in Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, whose late move to Chelsea was scuppered on deadline day, and the picture becomes further complicated.

Will Nyoni’s emergence as a genuine option lead Liverpool to quell their interest in the Senegalese? And what to be done with Szoboszlai and Gravenberch if so? It can’t be as simple as selling two of the highest earners, but then you also can’t have two of your highest earners on the bench, either. The midfield conundrum could define Iraola’s first season, and it might lead to a high-profile departure or two.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 18-year-old who has played at two major international tournaments and the division’s top clearance maker from last season also feature.

A tricky, exciting, quick and versatile midfielder, Azeez has proven himself in the Championship with Millwall over the past two seasons and now deserves a chance to test himself in the top flight.

In a recent development, brighton had been chasing him for a while and struck a deal on deadline day for a very reasonable reported initial £12.5m, rising to £15m. If he can make the step up and produce anything like his second-tier form, he’ll be a steal.

In a recent development, he is a high-volume producer at the sharp end of the pitch, constantly making things happen that threaten the opposition’s goal, but standing out most for his crossing. He ranked top of the Championship last season for open-play crosses (227) and expected assists from crosses (6.71 xA).

He also ranked fourth for dribble attempts (131), ninth for shots (95), sixth for chances created from open play (58). He created good-quality chances, too; only two players created more big chances than he did (18), and he ranked fourth for expected assists. His 9.12 xA alongside only seven assists suggests he may benefit from playing alongside better finishers.

A hugely exciting prospect. Despite being 18, Mbaye has significant and noteworthy experience under his belt. Last year he made six appearances, including in the final, for Senegal at the Africa Cup of Nations and this summer he made four appearances at the World Cup. He has also played in two Ligue 1 title-winning campaigns, including 2024-25, when he became the youngest player in PSG’s history to start a game, and won the Champions League in both of those seasons.

He is a dribbling and ball-carrying menace, who always looks as if he’s about to do something special. Among players to play at least 900 minutes in Ligue 1 last season, he was 11th for carries (moving at least five metres with the ball) per 90, with 20.0, and 12th for progressive carries (moving at least five metres upfield with the ball) per 90, with 10.3. Most of the players above him in both lists are defenders, who naturally have more space to move into.

In a recent development, he was third for take-on-ending carries, or running with the ball for at least five metres before attempting to beat an opponent with a dribble, with 2.9 per 90. And he also has end product to boot. He scored at Afcon and the World Cup despite limited minutes and his 0.45 goals or assists per 90 for PSG last season is not to be sniffed at.

Danso had a pretty impossible task over his two years at Tottenham. He was the back-up to the first-choice centre-backs Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven, playing intermittently on both sides of central defence in dysfunctional teams jumping between styles of play, and he very rarely played for any consistent run of games.

He was unfairly compared with the players he was replacing for much of his time there, but the truth is he was always reliable enough. He excelled, however, when Romero got injured during the run-in last season and he was called upon in Spurs’ time of need as they scraped clear of relegation.

He may not be the best on the ball – though he is hardly terrible – but he is an excellent deep defender. Among those to play at least 1,000 minutes in the Premier League last season, Danso ranked first for clearances (8.2 per 90) and headed clearances (6.3), and was fifth for aerial duels won (4.8 per 90).

Sources indicate that he could thrive at Sunderland, who spent more of their out-of-possession game time in a low block than any other team in the Premier League last season (25%). Danso could be perfectly at home in this setup, paired alongside the player he beat into second place for clearances and headed clearances: Dan Ballard.

It was always stated during Pep Guardiola’s time at Manchester City that attackers had their wings clipped in terms of individual freedom, limited to playing within the parameters of the manager’s meticulous gameplan.

But dribbling ability became increasingly crucial in the final years of his reign, with Jérémy Doku and Antoine Semenyo on the wings and Rayan Cherki in between. Doku (162) and Semenyo (144) ranked first and second for dribbles attempted in the Premier League last season, with Cherki ninth (111). They also ranked first (84), fourth (59) and eighth (51), respectively, for dribbles completed.

Sources indicate that with the deadline-day addition of Ndiaye, City have gone in even harder on dribbling ability under Enzo Maresca. The Senegal international ranked second for dribbles attempted (136) and dribbles completed (73) in the Premier League last season.

Fernandez-Pardo’s versatility is a major attraction. He’s comfortable playing off the left and cutting in on to his right foot, or as a No 9. Although not the bulkiest, he has explosive pace and promises to be a threat in behind.

The Belgium international is arguably at his most threatening when running with the ball because he does so with such purpose. His 122 carries progressing the ball at least 10 metres upfield in Ligue 1 last term were bettered by only seven players, several of whom were defenders.

On top of that, he ranked top for carries into the penalty area (69) and seventh for carries ending with a shot or chance created (39).

It has been revealed that fofana appeared to be enjoying a swift rise in 2024-25, only for a serious ankle injury to massively disrupt his development in 2025-26. Sunderland will be hoping they can get him back to the levels shown the season before last, when he was a real livewire on Lyon’s left flank.

Recent findings suggest that he contributed nine goal involvements (five goals, four assists) in 1,586 minutes in Ligue 1 in 2024-25, averaging one every 176 minutes. Only eight forwards (900+ mins) averaged more expected assists per 90 (0.25).

The most eye-catching aspects of his game, however, were his dynamism and pace. He could be difficult to stop once moving, and this made him a very useful outlet. Among Ligue 1 forwards (900+ mins), his 16.6 carries per 90 ranked him sixth, and he moved up to third for progressive carries per 90 (11.5).

Fofana is direct, exciting and has significant potential. He is a player Sunderland could make a profit on if he reaches the levels previously expected.

Andrés arrived to bolster Brighton’s midfield options after Carlos Baleba’s exit to Manchester United. Although a different type of midfielder to the Cameroonian, Chema is another with vast potential.

Industry observers note that A product of Real Madrid’s academy, Chema joined Stuttgart last summer. During his sole campaign in the Bundesliga, he was in and out of the team but caught the eye at the base of their midfield.

Industry observers note that comparisons have been made to Rodri because of his physical attributes and nominal role as a holding midfielder. He doesn’t have anything like the same influence in possession but Chema is tidy on the ball.

Sources indicate that it’s what he offers defensively that is most notable, however. He’s been broadly praised for his anticipation and reading of the game, ranking second among midfielders (900+ mins) since the start of last season for interceptions per 90 in the Bundesliga (2.3).

Dumbarton appoint 28-year-old manager.

Martin Fellowes has become the youngest manager in SPFL history, taking on the Dumbarton head coach job at the age of 28.

Leaving his position as assistant manager and head of football operations at Scottish League 2 leaders Stranraer, Fellowes inherits a team six places further down the ladder.

With experience on the Scotland Under-19s coaching team, Fellowes spent almost 10 years with East Kilbride, rising from teenage kit boy to a two-month spell as interim manager in 2023, winning the Lowland League Cup.

With a day job in office furniture sales, he holds a Uefa A licence.

"You have to earn people's respect as a person," Fellowes told BBC Scotland.

"When you are a young guy and you're leading a football club, I don't think you can come in and change everything and lead with an iron fist.

According to recent reports, "You have to get people's respect on and off the pitch. I know there will be plenty of criticism and there will be plenty of people sitting here today doubting that I'm capable of doing this job at 28.

"But now really the work for me has started on, by the end of the process, having gained those people onside to say, 'he was more than capable of doing this job and we're delighted to have him here'.

"I can only do that through winning games of football.".

Martin Fellowes (right) as a 17-year-old kit man at East Kilbride.

Jim Duffy was 29 when he began his long managerial career at Falkirk and Rhys McCabe was player/manager at Airdrieonians at the same age.

Ian Cathro, now leading French club Saint-Etienne, took charge of Hearts when he was just 30.

Fellowes replaces Frank McKeown, who resigned last month, while director of football Danny Lennon had been standing in on an interim basis.

The Sons are two points off the promotion places and visit Spartans on Saturday.

"We're not going to reinvent the wheel," Fellowes added.

"We're not going to do anything that anybody else hasn't been doing.

"But if we can add the 5% to every different department and win games of football, I think over time people will understand that sometimes the age isn't a barrier but it can actually be an advantage.".

East Fife sack Campbell as Lennon steps in at Dumbarton.

SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1122 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space
